label: Technology-neutral standards
basis: EPA names MEMA's technology-neutrality position in its summary and explains numeric performance-based standards without a ZEV mandate. MEMA itself describes the proposal as attempting performance-based standards. This is not proof of a new concession or full acceptance of every requested technology/incentive. No numeric stringency comparison was performed.

label: Joint Office coordination
basis: The reproduced original-page-4 recommendation seeks alignment with the Joint Office throughout implementation. Section 2.10 commits EPA and federal partners to continued engagement and monitoring, with referrals to section 2.9 and the final preamble. This supports broad coordination alignment, not a separate named MEMA disposition, complete alignment of regulations/priorities, or verified implementation.

label: Implementation-assumption monitoring
basis: MEMA asks EPA to follow through on critical-material, infrastructure and milestone assumptions and take action to realize them. The final preamble specifies data collection, reports and consultation about infrastructure and battery/material supply. EPA leaves later guidance, rulemaking or no change open. Monitoring is aligned with part of the request but is not a guarantee of all assumed outcomes or an automatic standards adjustment.

label: Cleaner-combustion/fuel incentives
basis: The reproduced recommendations request cleaner-combustion/fuel incentives. EPA describes technology choices, conditional alternative-fuel tailpipe credit and GEM pathways, while declining the new H2ICE multiplier separately coded at r30. Existing eligibility, fuel approval and retained approaches do not establish a blanket new incentive or another independent policy event.

label: Alternative-fuel analysis
basis: The original and reproduced paragraph ask for more analysis of hydrogen, ethanol, renewable natural gas and renewable diesel. The reviewed general response explains pathways and rule scope; it does not verify completion of the requested comparative analysis. Referenced regulatory-impact-analysis chapters were not independently reviewed.

label: Renewable-diesel compliance option
basis: The original footnote and reproduced excerpt cite CARB's In-Use Off-Road Diesel-Fueled Fleets Regulation section 2449.1(f), but the later summary groups MEMA with cap-and-trade and the Low Carbon Fuel Standard. The general response explains conditional exhaust-CO2 credits and declines a lifecycle/fuel-regulatory alternative within this rule. It does not separately decide the exact cited off-road provision. Neither blanket renewable-diesel prohibition nor a new CARB-style compliance provision is established.

label: Lifecycle-carbon assessment
basis: MEMA asks for broader assessment of vehicle/component production and charging emissions, not only a lifecycle-based standard. Section 17.1's general response retains vehicle-based standard setting and discusses upstream attribution limitations. Section 9.3 discusses hydrogen-production comparisons and refers to RIA 4.8, which was not independently reviewed. This supports a standards-scope response, not a claim EPA ignored all upstream emissions or completed the full requested assessment.

label: Four-year implementation lead
basis: The section reproduces MEMA's request. Its general response rejects the claimed statutory minimum, explicitly addressing EMA rather than MEMA by name, while agreeing that some categories need more time. The final preamble retains 2027 for some vehicles and describes category-specific delays, not a uniform four-year rule.

label: Transition-disruption cost accounting
basis: The original note and agency excerpt agree on the conditional year. The complete timing response discusses reasonable costs and other commenters' cost objections, but does not separately establish addition of the specified facility, financial and scheduling burdens. Its referrals to preamble and RIA cost analyses are not a verified cost-model change.

label: Battery end-of-life costs
basis: MEMA's request is reproduced twice and summarized by name. The recycling response refers to broader analysis, and the mineral-security paragraphs discuss recycling supply and funding. These passages do not establish addition of the requested recycling/disposal costs. The RIA explicitly reports a different addition: battery-replacement and ICE-rebuild purchaser costs.

label: Material-availability sensitivity analysis
basis: The collective response acknowledges uncertainty, rejects projected mineral-shortfall objections and cites a new ANL analysis. The final preamble adds BMI lithium scenarios with project-stage weighting. This partly aligns with the requested method changes, but does not verify the full scaling/confidence/sensitivity request or attribute changes to MEMA.

label: Fleet infrastructure partnerships
basis: EPA describes existing grants, tax credits and stakeholder engagement. These support the infrastructure theme but do not separately verify the specific new government/fleet partnership requested by MEMA.

label: Hydrogen-timeline reconciliation
basis: EPA names MEMA and distinguishes current-network figures, production scenarios and early-market actions from a requirement for a complete national network. This is a documented response disputing the claimed mismatch, not independent confirmation that the Roadmap, forecasts or actual deployment align.

label: Interstate charging/refueling funding
basis: Original page 9 requests additional interstate infrastructure and increased hydrogen/DCFC funding targets. Section 2.10 commits coordination; sections 6.1 and 6.4 describe existing funding, freight-corridor planning and infrastructure investment. These passages do not establish a new allocation or increased funding target answering MEMA's request. They also do not establish no funding was awarded elsewhere.

label: ATRI-study inclusion
basis: The original request seeks consideration of the December 2022 ATRI infrastructure study. Its reproduced appendix map is explicitly full-fleet. Response A discusses ATA/ATRI estimates and cites that study at footnote 578, but distinguishes complete electrification from EPA's modeled rule pathway. This verifies engagement with the requested study, not adoption of its numbers as the rule's impact.

label: Bidirectional fast-charging grants
basis: PDF 875 reproduces the specific public-purchase recommendation from original page 10. PDF 987 separately reproduces its page-9/10 rationale, not the grant criterion. Section 6.4 names MEMA among future-proofing commenters, acknowledges potential V2G benefits and says those benefits were not quantitatively included in the rule analysis. Agreement with benefits and descriptions of existing programs do not verify adoption of a DCFC/bidirectional public-funding criterion.

label: ACT bus-forecast acquisition
basis: No separate disposition of the bus-report acquisition request was located in the reviewed section-6.1 response or section-3.1 sales-distribution response. Section 3.1 describes revised fleet composition in a summary naming AVE and MFN, not MEMA. The opening response paragraph on PDF 735 separately changes adoption-bin inputs from ACT Research to NREL TEMPO. Neither update establishes acquisition, use or rejection of the requested bus-market forecasts. Source-reported shares are not independently reproduced calculations.

label: Public readiness dashboard
basis: The original-page-10 dashboard request is reproduced in section 6.1. That response promises periodic reports. The final preamble specifies collection and consultation but does not separately adopt the requested Joint Office dashboard in the compared passages. Section 6.4's public-information response begins by naming DTNA; its refusal of mandatory infrastructure reporting must not be recoded as a named refusal of MEMA's dashboard.

label: Federal/state/local infrastructure coordination
basis: The request on original page 11 is reproduced. EPA commits to stakeholder engagement and describes federal coordination and corridor planning. This supports broad alignment, without verifying every state/local action or actual implementation.

label: Advance utility buildout
basis: EPA discusses investments, utility planning and anticipated demand. In these reviewed responses it does not establish a requirement compelling utilities to build ahead of demand. This is a scope-limited unresolved instrument, not a finding that no utility action occurred.

label: Workforce/capital-plan alignment
basis: EPA lists workforce programs and refers to employment responses. The section 6.4 workforce summary names South Coast AQMD, not MEMA. Training support does not verify alignment of workforce development and incentives with end-user capital plans; the full employment chapter and implementation records were not audited.

label: Charger lifecycle standards
basis: MEMA's original recommendation concerns national installation, operation and maintenance standards. The section-6.4 summary groups MEMA with MECA on minimum charger efficiency, while the reproduced MECA excerpt contains that specific efficiency request. The general responses cite FHWA's existing NEVI standards, reliability efforts and voluntary EnergyStar certification. These provide thematic context but do not separately establish full adoption of MEMA's broader lifecycle-standardization request.

label: Charging cybersecurity standards
basis: The original-page-11 EV/EVSE cybersecurity recommendation and page-12 risk reference are reproduced. The complete section-6.1 and section-6.4 general responses discuss charging availability, reliability, efficiency and coordination without a separate disposition of this cybersecurity-policy request. Reliability or V2G national-security benefits are not a cybersecurity standard. This is bounded nonresolution, not docket-wide nonresponse.

label: Lightweighting input refresh
basis: The named response directs MEMA to an existing approval route for weight reductions not covered by the standard inputs. The proposal and April 2024 final publication retain all six later-phase wheel values and all 22 nonwheel component/material rows in Tables 6 and 8. Table headings change from Phase 2 and Phase 3 to Phase 2 and later, so this is not a byte-identical text finding. Retention is consistent with r25 but supplies neither a new grant of credits nor the requested r24 default refresh or supplier consultation.

label: Lightweighting credit retention
basis: The named response directs MEMA to an existing approval route for weight reductions not covered by the standard inputs. The proposal and April 2024 final publication retain all six later-phase wheel values and all 22 nonwheel component/material rows in Tables 6 and 8. Table headings change from Phase 2 and Phase 3 to Phase 2 and later, so this is not a byte-identical text finding. Retention is consistent with r25 but supplies neither a new grant of credits nor the requested r24 default refresh or supplier consultation.

label: Warranty repair-location clarification
basis: EPA names MEMA and points to 40 CFR 1037.125(f); this coding records EPA's explanation, not a newly granted repair right.

label: Warranty component specification
basis: EPA refers the named group to III.B.2; the preamble specifies battery and associated powertrain coverage, including inverters and fuel-cell stacks. Specification does not equal the requested narrow scope.

label: Wear/adjacent-component warranty exclusions
basis: The reviewed preamble/clauses retain broader coverage and manufacturer-defined covered failures. They do not establish a blanket wear/adjacency exception or adjudicate every example separately.

label: Supplier-informed warranty exclusion list
basis: The original and reproduced excerpt contain this process request; the reviewed summary, response and preamble do not separately decide it. This is not docket-wide nonresponse or rejection.

label: H2ICE multiplier extension
basis: Section 9.3 explicitly disagrees with MEMA's new H2ICE multiplier request; section 10.3.1 names MEMA among the requesting organizations and declines a new multiplier because that extension was outside the reopened scope. Both scoped multiplier clauses enumerate PHEV, BEV and FCEV, not a new H2ICE multiplier. This is a documented refusal, not a missing response.

label: FCEV multiplier retention
basis: The proposal already retained the 5.5 FCEV generation multiplier through MY2027. The final generation provision retains it, but the multiplier-credit use rules restrict Phase 3 use in MY2027-2029 and prohibit certification use from MY2030. The final also retains PHEV/BEV generation through MY2027, unlike the proposed earlier phase-out; that separate change is not attributed to MEMA's FCEV retention request. Generation, use and base credits are distinct.

label: H2ICE zero-CO2 treatment retention
basis: MEMA explicitly supports the proposed vehicle/GEM zero-CO2 treatment. Proposed and final section 1037.150(f) have the same relevant clause for neat-hydrogen vehicles, and the final preamble distinguishes vehicle certification from the engine program. This is retained proposal alignment, not a newly caused concession, a full ZEV definition, zero for all pollutants or zero for all hydrogen blends. The separate engine default is optional and has a different unit.

label: Broader CARB exceptions
basis: The original and reproduced text ask EPA to encourage broader CARB exceptions; the section-9.3 summary names MEMA. The complete general response in that section does not separately commit to the requested state engagement. Federal testing treatment and EPA's response to CARB's own position are not this requested action. This is not docket-wide nonresponse, rejection, or proof that no interagency action occurred.

label: Broader vocational duty-cycle inputs
basis: EPA explains that its sources cover more than utility boom trucks and defends nationwide FleetDNA, UC Riverside and MOVES data against individual-manufacturer datasets. The specific PTO change is recorded under r35. These passages do not verify adoption of all offered GPS, route, elevation and vocational datasets.

label: PTO input expansion
basis: EPA explicitly says it averaged MEMA's submitted concrete-mixer range to increase PTO inputs. RIA PDF 236, printed 211, reports 42% for cement mixer/pumper in Table 2-17; PDF 237, printed 212, assigns 42% to 19C_Mix_Cl8_MP in Table 2-18. This confirms documentary input uptake, not every requested PTO expansion, implementation in an executed model, measured lobbying power or a real-world causal effect.

label: Higher-power charging sensitivity
basis: The actual MEMA sensitivity request is reproduced on PDF 950. The summary and response on 946-948 instead name TRALA when discussing the same kind of sensitivity. EPA explicitly says it did not conduct the HD TRUCS sensitivity. This is thematic non-adoption of the requested analysis, not a named rejection of MEMA; no equivalence of complete MEMA and TRALA submissions is asserted.

label: Dwell/charger-intention data solicitation
basis: The request is reproduced, but the reviewed responses do not separately dispose of MEMA's public information solicitation. EPA reports commissioned NREL dwell-time analysis and revised charger sharing; analysis of existing data does not verify a new public RFI about dwell times and charger intentions. No rejection or docket-wide nonresponse is coded.

label: Renewed technical-data consultation
basis: EPA summarizes MEMA's procedural request and explicitly disagrees with opening a second comment period because additional PTO data had already been solicited. The alternative technical-amendment route in MEMA's original is not separately resolved in this response.

label: Slower specialized-vehicle adoption projections
basis: EPA names MEMA and explains a more gradual early phase-in, especially for heavy vocational vehicles, in light of manufacturer resources and infrastructure. This partly aligns with specialization concerns, without verifying a blanket delay for every specialized application. The broader timing change shares the existing timing-ledger comparison and is not a new independent event.

label: Body-builder accessory electrification credits
basis: The original page-18 request includes body builders and accessory electrification after chassis delivery. The reviewed responses describe existing ePTO provisions. The vehicle-application summary attributes a delegated-assembler credit request to NTEA, while PTO excerpts include Odyne. Neither is substituted for a named MEMA response. A new body-builder route or GEM feature is not verified.

label: Variable-worksite fuel-option modeling
basis: EPA summarizes MEMA's requested liquid/renewable-fuel modeling, then states it did not explicitly model liquid hydrogen and assessed gaseous tanks instead. This resolves that component at documentary scope. It does not establish a prohibition on liquid-hydrogen compliance or separately settle every renewable fuel and variable-worksite application requested.

label: Emergency-utility BEV opposition
basis: EPA explicitly links additional regional utility-truck modeling limits to MEMA and similar comments: zero modeled ZEV adoption in MY2027 and a 14% limit in MY2030/MY2032. Urban and multi-purpose utility uses are distinguished. The 100-mile minimum range change is discussed separately in response to POET and must not be solely attributed to MEMA. These are model assumptions, not observed adoption or a blanket ban.

label: Emergency custom-chassis certification extension
basis: EPA names the requested emergency-category extension in its summary, then says it retains the existing eight custom-chassis categories. This does not verify the requested additional emergency category. The operative clauses and category definitions were not independently compared in this follow-up; do not turn this collective response into an explicit named refusal or infer that existing categories never cover emergency uses.

label: Mission-productivity modeling
basis: EPA reproduces the non-emergency mission-productivity request. Its responses discuss payload, battery sizing, daily VMT, extremes and ICE alternatives but do not separately establish the requested mission-productivity factor. Related modeling changes are not evidence of full one-for-one replacement or acceptance of this specific instrument.

label: Early-adopter readiness reassessment
basis: EPA reproduces the request and acknowledges depot suitability for school buses, transit buses and port drayage. The general response retains depot modeling and adds selected public charging; elsewhere it explains no separate drayage standard. These passages do not separately verify the requested reassessment for all three advanced applications or assign resulting changes to MEMA.

label: AB2127 implementation review
basis: PDF 877 points readers to MEMA Appendix 2 on original pages 24-26 without reproducing the page-25 AB2127 recommendation. Coordination and best-practice discussion in reviewed responses does not verify review of that specific program. A CARB footnote to AB2127 is not a MEMA request-response match.

label: State MHDV charging requirements
basis: The actual request appears on original page 26; PDF 877 only refers to Appendix 2. EPA discusses distinct HD charging needs, existing NEVI programs and state guidance, including that states need not use NEVI funds for HD charging. These responses do not verify new EPA charging requirements for ACT and non-ACT states.

label: FHWA truck/bus charging guidance
basis: The actual request appears on original page 26; PDF 877 only refers to Appendix 2. EPA describes existing FHWA guidance encouraging future HD needs and a 2023 rule that does not specifically accommodate HD charging. This is not verification of new EPA-provided truck/bus guidance or of MEMA causing the already-existing guidance.
